newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Meridor seeks greater trade with Jordan.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Meridor seeks greater trade with Jordan.

text.p: Israeli Finance Minister Dan Meridor said on Monday that he was trying to ease administrative trade barriers between Israel and Jordan and between the West Bank and Gaza Strip.
Speaking at a seminar on Middle East business Meridor said he wanted to allow Israeli and Jordanian trucks to travel to each other's countries.

"There are problems on the bridges (linking Jordan and Israel). I have heard from Israelis who want to trade with Jordan it takes too much time to go back-to-back from lorry to lorry. I am trying to get these things changed," he said.
Meridor said he had raised the issue with security officials.

With regard to the Palestinian self-rule areas, Meridor indicated he wanted to do away with licences now required from Palestinians traveling between the West Bank and Gaza. "I have always found it very strange that a Palestinian can go from Nablus (in the West Bank) to Tel Aviv without any problem but he needs a licence to go to Gaza," Meridor said.

He also said he had doubts about the effectiveness of the closure on the Palestinian areas, which Israel imposed in February in the midst of suicide bombings by Moslem militants opposed to the peace process.
On Sunday thousands of Palestinian workers returned to their jobs in Israel when the Jewish state eased the closure.

Meridor called on Israeli industrialists not to block imports from Jordan and Egypt. "I think it is the role of the government to stop protecting industries and allow cheaper products in the country," Meridor said. "We are not competing but complementary markets."
Meridor also expressed disappointment with the extent of Israel's trade relations with Eygpt and said much more progress had been made with Jordan.
When asked about opposition in Jordan to doing business with Israel, Meridor replied: "I don't think the situation is equal to the one in Egypt."
